name: Antonio del Valle Perochena
current_role: Lead Director, Byline Bancorp (director since 2013); Chairman, Kaluz S.A. and Grupo Financiero Ve por Más (BX+)
profile: Mexican businessman, son of Antonio del Valle Ruiz. Chairs family holding company Kaluz (controlling shareholder of Orbia Advance Corp.) and BX+ bank; Orbia board member since 2002. Has sat on Chicago-based Byline Bancorp's board since June 2013 and became Lead Director in Feb 2021; a ~25% holder via MBG Investors.
interesting_fact: Served four years as president of the Mexican Business Council (CMN), which groups about 60 of Mexico's most important companies, ending his term in 2023.

public_contacts.value: brennie@bylinebank.com (Brooks O. Rennie, Head of IR, Byline Bank - listed as investors/media contact)

notes: Sources conflict on Orbia chairmanship: Orbia's own governance page lists his brother Juan Pablo del Valle Perochena as Orbia chairman; Antonio chairs Kaluz. Role facts from Byline 2026 proxy (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001702750/000119312526162758/by-20260417.htm). Orbia (PVC/fluor/pipes) is relevant to energy/infrastructure.

name: Han Wenchen
current_role: President, Baoye Group (宝业集团), Tangshan, Hebei (per ifeng profile; date not stated)
profile: Hebei steel entrepreneur born Dec 1957. Per Qianzhan profile, worked as a coal miner and in transport, then opened coal mines; his father founded the Banbidian steel group in 1987, which became private Baoye Group in 2001. President since April 2000; group spans steel, real estate, coal, transport and trade.
interesting_fact: Former deputy to the 10th Hebei Provincial People's Congress and recipient of the national 'May Day' Labour Medal; deputy Party secretary of Tangshan's Banbidian village.
deep_cut_fact: Started out as a coal miner and in the transport business before opening his own coal mines to build capital.
notes: Not the same as HK-listed Baoye Group (2355.HK, Zhejiang construction). Hurun listing 2003-2008 only; current status unverified.

name: Liu Zhixin
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Ficont (中际联合), Shanghai-listed - largest shareholder (~39.5% per 36Kr)
profile: Founder-chairman of Ficont, which started selling suspended work platforms overseas and around 2008 pivoted to high-altitude safety equipment (tower lifts, ladders, fall protection) for wind turbines under the '3S Lift' brand. Listed on the Shanghai main board in May 2021.
interesting_fact: Ficont's wind-turbine work-at-height safety equipment held about two-thirds of the China market in 2019, per a Shanghai Securities News interview with Liu at the 2021 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: The company's '3S Lift' brand stands for Safe, Simple, Specialized.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (wind-power O&M equipment). Shares Hurun listing with Yu Haiyan. 36Kr source: https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/1678253559985159

name: Fan Shaowen
current_role: Chairman, general manager and legal representative, Chengdu Olymvax Biopharmaceuticals (欧林生物, STAR 688319)
profile: Born 1953; trained in regional economics at Southwest Normal University. Spent 1976-91 at the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences' Institute of Blood Transfusion, then Shuyang Pharma, Chongqing Dalin Biotech and Wuhan Ruide. Founded human-vaccine maker Olymvax in 2009 at age 56; daughter Fan Fan is vice-chair. Olymvax filed for a HK listing in Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: Founded his vaccine company at 56, after more than 30 years in blood-product and biotech roles.
deep_cut_fact: Headed the protein laboratory at the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences' Institute of Blood Transfusion from 1976 to 1991; he is a licensed pharmacist and chief technician.
notes: Career details from Chinese media summaries; verify against Olymvax annual report.

name: Andy Jassy
profile: Grew up in Scarsdale, NY; Harvard AB and MBA. Joined Amazon in 1997 as a marketing manager, was Jeff Bezos's first technical adviser, conceived AWS with Bezos in 2003 and led it from its 57-person original team; succeeded Bezos as Amazon CEO in July 2021.
interesting_fact: Minority owner of the NHL's Seattle Kraken (joined the ownership group in 2018) and chairs the board of Rainier Prep charter school in Seattle.
deep_cut_fact: Wanted to be a sportscaster: spent three college summers at New York's Fox affiliate on the launch of 'Good Day New York', covering Mets batting practice; sent his reel to ~200 TV markets, got two offers, declined them. Later worked at a retail golf store, which taught him 'a ton'.
notes: Highly relevant (AWS / data centers). Best route is Amazon corporate communications.

profile: Signs Joy Kie's annual reports as company head and is one of its three controlling shareholders/actual controllers (with Lu Zhiyong and Li Yuguang) under an acting-in-concert agreement renewed Aug 2026. Joy Kie is a Hangzhou-based bicycle exporter.

name: Lin Heping
current_role: Senior technical adviser, Fujian Niaowang (鸟王) Shoes; vice chairman, China Leather Industry Association (per 2020 report)
profile: Born 1957 in Shishi, Fujian; co-founded shoe brand Fuguiniao (富贵鸟) with cousins from a 1984 souvenir workshop, building it to 10,000+ staff and 3,000+ stores. After Fuguiniao's 2019 delisting and sale, he returned to the craft as a shoemaker/technical adviser.
interesting_fact: Fuguiniao was named the first 'China Shoe King' in 1993.
deep_cut_fact: Now works hands-on in a sub-40-square-metre sample-making workshop as a shoemaker.
notes: Former company went bankrupt; avoid referencing it negatively. Alive status inferred from 2020 reporting.

name: P Prathap Reddy
current_role: Founder, Penna Cement Industries (sold to Adani's Ambuja Cements, 2024)
profile: Puttamreddy Prathap Reddy founded Hyderabad-based Penna Cement around 1991 and ran it as chairman & MD. In June 2024 his family's promoter group agreed to sell 100% of Penna to Ambuja Cements at an enterprise value of Rs 10,422 crore (~14 MTPA capacity).
interesting_fact: Sold Penna Cement to the Adani Group's Ambuja Cements in a Rs 10,422 crore deal in 2024.
notes: Education (Pachaiyappa's College) only from MarketScreener aggregator. Current role after sale unclear.

name: Sacha Mascolo-Tarbuck
current_role: Global Brand Director & Owner, TONI&GUY Global Group; majority/controlling shareholder (June 2026); sole owner of label.m
profile: Daughter of TONI&GUY co-founder Toni Mascolo. Long-time global creative director responsible for the brand's imagery and annual trend collections; in June 2026 took a majority controlling stake in TONI&GUY Global Group, with label.m wholly owned by her.
interesting_fact: Her grandfather Francesco was a barber from near Pompeii; her father and uncle opened the first TONI&GUY salon in Clapham, London.
deep_cut_fact: Started out assisting her uncle Anthony on brand-building, and helped session stylist Guido Paulo at London Fashion Week creating big 1980s hair for supermodels; says 'I'm a fashion follower rather than celebrity lover.'
notes: Ownership news: https://hji.co.uk/toniguy-global-group-enters-new-era (8 June 2026). Off-topic for energy podcast; entrepreneurship angle only.

name: Chandu Virani
current_role: Founder and director, Balaji Wafers Pvt Ltd, Rajkot
profile: From a farming family in Jamnagar district, Gujarat; moved to Rajkot in 1974 and worked in a cinema canteen. Began making potato wafers in 1982 with Rs 10,000, opened a factory in 1989 and built Balaji Wafers into a major Indian snack brand, turning down offers from PepsiCo, General Mills and ~50 PE firms.
interesting_fact: Worked at Rajkot's Astron Cinema canteen for Rs 90 a month, also pasting posters and ushering; the Balaji name came from a temple at the cinema premises.
deep_cut_fact: Repaired torn cinema seats at night in exchange for a snack and chutney; says 'No one in the family till date knows how to fry wafers except me.'
notes: Alive status not explicitly confirmed by a recent source.

name: Alex Langsam
current_role: Founder, chief executive and largest shareholder, Britannia Hotels
profile: Born June 1938 in Vienna, family settled in Hove, England. Former estate agent/property developer; bought the derelict Country House Hotel in Didsbury, Manchester in 1976, renaming it the Britannia Hotel, and built the chain (incl. Adelphi Liverpool, Grand Scarborough); bought Pontins in 2011, saving 850 jobs.
interesting_fact: In 1982 he acquired the assets of British Transport Hotels, British Rail's hotel division.
deep_cut_fact: Studied economics at Aberystwyth, which he said was 'the only institution that would allow him to study without an O-Level in mathematics.'
notes: Media-shy; company has drawn negative press. Alive per Wikipedia 'Living people'.

current_role: Co-founder, co-chairman and president, Tuya Inc. (NYSE: TUYA; HKEX: 2391)
profile: Leo Chen is founder/co-founder and president of IoT smart-device platform Tuya. Previously co-founded PHPWind and was an operations director at Alibaba (2008-2014), incl. Alibaba Cloud OS operations. Tuya is dual-listed in New York and Hong Kong.
interesting_fact: Before Tuya he co-founded PHPWind, and in 2015 was described as a former Alibaba Cloud OS operations director turned Tuya president.
